{{short description|Hungarian mathematician}}
'''Bálint Virág''' {{post-nominals|country=CAN|FRSC}} (born 1973) is a [[Hungary|Hungarian]] [[mathematician]] working in [[Canada]], known for his work in [[probability theory]], particularly determinantal processes, [[random matrix]] theory, and [[random walk]]s and other probabilistic questions on [[group theory|group]]s. He received his Ph.D. from [[U.C. Berkeley]] in 2000, under the direction of [[Yuval Peres]],<ref>{{mathgenealogy|id=44669}}</ref> and was a post-doc at [[MIT]]. Since 2003 he has been a [[Canada research chair]] at the [[University of Toronto]].

Virág was awarded a [[Sloan Fellowship]] (2004), the [[Rollo Davidson Prize]]<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.statslab.cam.ac.uk/Rollo/index.html |title=Rollo Davidson Prize |access-date=2010-04-27 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120118142455/http://www.statslab.cam.ac.uk/Rollo/index.html |archive-date=2012-01-18 |url-status=dead }}</ref> (2008), the [[Coxeter–James Prize]]<ref>[http://www.math.ca/MediaReleases/2010/cj-announcement 2010 Coxeter–James Prize announcement]</ref> (2010), and the [[John L. Synge Award]] (2014).<ref>{{citation|url=https://www.ams.org/notices/201411/rnoti-p1359.pdf|department=Mathematics People|journal=[[Notices of the American Mathematical Society]]|date=December 2014|title=Virag Receives Synge Award|page=1359|volume=61|issue=11}}.</ref> He was an [[list of International Congresses of Mathematicians Plenary and Invited Speakers|invited speaker at the International Congress of Mathematicians]] in 2014.<ref>{{citation|url=http://www.mathunion.org/db/ICM/Speakers/SortedByLastname.php|title=ICM Plenary and Invited Speakers since 1897|publisher=[[International Mathematical Union]]|accessdate=2015-10-10|archive-date=2017-11-24|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171124141541/http://www.mathunion.org/db/ICM/Speakers/SortedByLastname.php|url-status=dead}}.</ref> In 2024, he was named a [[Fellow of the Royal Society of Canada]].<ref>{{citation|url=https://www.mathematics.utoronto.ca/news/bálint-virág-named-2024-fellow-royal-society-canada|title=Bálint Virág named 2024 Fellow of the Royal Society of Canada |
access-date=2026-09-03 | website=www.mathematics.utoronto.ca}}.</ref>
